key_question_a_answer.answer: BOTH, but the dominant failure is Tier-1 gutter detection producing wrong column boundaries — not Tier-0 over-classification and not Tier-2 label attachment.

tier_0_grouping_failure_analysis.expected: Pages 3, 4, 5, 6 should form ONE logical unit (balance sheet: assets p3-4, liabilities p5-6). Schema-page = 3. Pages 4, 5, 6 should be continuation pages inheriting p3 schema.
tier_0_grouping_failure_analysis.actual: Each of pages 3, 4, 5, 6 is its own unit with is_schema_page=1, schema_inherited_from_page=null.
tier_0_grouping_failure_analysis.root_cause: The Tier-0 fingerprint-continuity test uses gutter_x_positions (as fractions) with a GUTTER_POSITION_TOLERANCE of 5% of page width. Page 3 has gutters at [0, 0.97, 0.99]. Page 4 has gutters at [0, 0.02, 0.03]. The gutter positions differ by 0.95 (95% of page width) — far beyond 5% tolerance. The grouping algorithm correctly applies the continuity rule, but the gutter DETECTION itself is producing wildly different gutter positions for consecutive balance-sheet pages that are physically the same document section. This is a Tier-1 per-page gutter-detection failure that cascades into Tier-0 grouping failure: because each page detects different gutter positions, the continuity test always breaks, making every page its own schema-page unit. The schema-inheritance architecture is sound but is never triggered because grouping never fires.

root_cause_verdict.primary_bug: Tier-1 gutter detection (in infrastructure/generic_md_table_extractor.py) produces inconsistent and wrong gutter positions across consecutive pages of the same balance-sheet section. Pages 3 and 5 detect gutters at [0, 0.97, 0.99] (two 22-25px slivers at far right), page 4 detects gutters at [0, 0.02, 0.03] (two 25-29px slivers at far LEFT), page 6 detects no gutters at all. These wildly different fingerprints prevent Tier-0 from grouping them into one unit, so schema inheritance is never applied.
root_cause_verdict.secondary_bug: Even where schema inheritance IS triggered (pages 9-10, 18-19), the inherited gutter positions are themselves wrong — all content lands in one dominant column, with value columns either absent or in slivers. So the schema inheritance mechanism works mechanically but inherits a bad schema.
root_cause_verdict.gate_status: The Tier-3 invariant gate is WORKING CORRECTLY as a detector — it correctly quarantines 12 of 18 units. The gate is catching bad extraction. However, Invariant 3 (no-orphan-row) has a leniency gap: when ALL content is dumped into one wide column (as in pages 3, 5 with col_2 spanning 25px), the gate classifies rows as 'junk' (label=null) but when the wide column is col_0 or col_2 with text content, it passes as 'label present + value present.' This allowed page 4 to pass despite being structurally scrambled.

zone_ownership.tier_0_grouping: apps/pdf-extractor/infrastructure/generic_md_table_extractor.py — build_document_map() function. The gutter continuity test is logically correct but the per-page fingerprints it receives are garbage.
zone_ownership.tier_1_gutter_detection: apps/pdf-extractor/infrastructure/generic_md_table_extractor.py — zone_page() function. The projection-profile based column gutter detection is failing systematically: it is detecting false gutters at the extreme margins of the page (narrow slivers) rather than the actual inter-column whitespace. This is the root defect.

verdict_rationale: 33.3% pass rate (6/18 units) breaches the >50% done-bar (Decision F). Excluding 3 trivially-passing prose units (pages 1, 2, 11 with row_count=0): 3 content-bearing units pass out of 15 = 20% on content units. The done-bar is not close to being met. The regression check page (page 5, NGUON VON / liabilities) is quarantined AND even its stitched content is structurally scrambled. AC-LFE-2 (page 5 inherits from page 3) FAILS — page 5 is its own unit with no schema inheritance. The gate correctly caught bad extraction (good: the gate works). One passing unit (page 4) is structurally wrong but gate-passing due to Invariant 3 leniency (bad: gate needs tightening for the all-content-in-one-column case).

gate_assessment.leniency_gap_detail: Invariant 3 passes page 4 whose entire row content is in one wide column (labels+values+codes mashed together). A row with col_0=empty, col_1=empty, col_2='label value1 value2 code' passes because col_2 has non-null content with text. The invariant should additionally require that the label column and at least one value column are DISTINCT non-empty cells, not just that 'some column has content.'

next.fix_description: The projection-profile horizontal gutter detection is placing gutters at the page margins (1-3% and 97-99% of page width) rather than in actual inter-column whitespace. Fix must produce gutters that correctly separate the label column (~0-35% of page width), the code column (~35-45%), and the value columns (~45-75% and 75-100%). Additionally, the Tier-0 grouping continuity test tolerance (5%) may need recalibration once gutter positions are corrected, as the current wide variance is gutter-detection noise, not real structural difference.
next.also_fix: Invariant 3 leniency gap — require distinct non-empty label cell AND distinct non-empty value cell, not just 'some column has content'
next.do_not_touch: Schema inheritance mechanism (pages 9-10 proof shows it works correctly when gutter positions are consistent). Tier-0 grouping logic is architecturally correct. text_table_extractor.py (0-byte-diff constraint).
